newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm,unaffected by IMF unreadiness.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm,unaffected by IMF unreadiness.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds rose on Tuesday and dealers said news the International Monetary Fund had delayed its recommendation to release a new tranche of the loan to Russia had little impact on the market.

The IMF Moscow representative said on Tuesday the fund is not yet ready to recommend releasing a new tranche of its $10 billion three-year loan to Russia, but experts will return soon to talk further.
"Bids were hit at once but it does not mean a correction has started -- buying has resumed," an ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said.
Dealers said rumours about the news had been already expected by the market and prices fell just 0.20 point at most.
"Buying interest is constant from the West as they could expect narrower spreads between MinFins and U.S. Treasuries," one dealer said.
The ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said: "Russia is going up and the trend is likely to continue these days ahead of the issue of new Eurobonds."
Russia is launching the second tranche of its Eurobond in March, with the volume up to 1.5 billion marks. The road-show schedule is to be announced this week.
Dealers said trading in the sixth and seventh tranches, usually illiquid among Russian operators, had been more active for the last few weeks on the both sides of the market.
